_comment: The post metadata that is NOT the post: the SEO description and the
details block, shared by postroll/blog_meta.py and
PostRollApp/Sources/Services/BlogMeta.swift (#283).
Why it exists at all: every generated post ships
<meta name="description" content="">, so Squarespace falls back to
og:description, which takes the opening prose. The summary search engines
and AI crawlers see for the Whitacre post is 'The hall wasn't open yet.
Singers in black were already out on 57th Street...'. Good writing,
useless as a summary.
Why deterministic rather than model written: neither string may live
inside the post body, because _fix_missing_contractions would send the
details block to Claude to be reworded (it has no contraction), the
second-person guard exempts only the LAST prose paragraph so a block after
the CTA makes the guard start rewriting the closing line, and
blog_quality counts any non-[PHOTO: block as prose so its invented-number
check flags the date. Separate fields, rendered at copy and export time,
never entering the AI round trip.
The rules both implementations satisfy:
1. The description opens with what was photographed, which follows the
shoot type, because the prose has to match what Dan actually
witnessed.
2. An org with the same name as the event is dropped, the same rule
media/brand_text.detail_lines already applies: it is already the
title, so repeating it is noise.
An org with the same name as the VENUE is dropped too, which is every
resident company at its own theater.
3. A missing org, venue, room or name drops its clause rather than
leaving a string with a hole in it.
4. The description is always inside Squarespace's 50 to 300 band. An
over-long one sheds the room, then the org, then truncates the event
name at a word boundary. It never ships out of band.
5. Em and en dashes are stripped: spaced ones become a comma, tight ones
become a space. Written here as escapes so the repo's own style hook
has nothing to catch.
6. The details block omits a line it has no value for, never printing a
label with nothing after it.
Dates arrive as ISO strings and render through a hardcoded month table in
both languages rather than a locale formatter, because a locale-dependent
month name is exactly the kind of drift this file exists to prevent.
The over-long vector's description was MEASURED by running seo_description, not written by hand, so this file cannot record a trim the real function does not produce.

_dates_comment: #1106: format_date and BlogMeta.formatDate are twins found by name, not
by anybody declaring them. They were covered only through the details
block above, so a disagreement about a single date would have shown up as
a whole details block mismatch and been read as a details bug.
Every valid ISO date the two must render identically. The months are here
because both sides carry their own list of them, which is two places for
_bad_dates_comment: What each side does with a date it cannot read, which is where they
deliberately DIFFER and the difference is the point (L542). Python raises,
because it generates the post and a malformed date reaching the
description would be published as the summary. Swift returns an empty
string, because it renders a screen and a trap there takes the app down.
Recorded rather than reconciled: making them agree would either publish a
bad date or crash the app.
